topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing and pedagogical context for the lecture on complement.

topics.label: Foundational principles and central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the core organization, naming conventions, and central C3-driven mechanism of the complement cascade.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three distinct upstream recognition pathways that drive complement deposition and converge to reach the trigger threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream functional mechanisms through which activated complement mediates immune defense and pathogen destruction.

topics.label: Regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how host regulatory proteins inhibit complement activation to protect healthy self cells from damage.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the distinct pathological presentations and clinical conditions caused by deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the molecular strategies evolved by pathogens to evade complement recognition and destruction.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the presentation on complement and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
